# Acceptance rule: what blocks acceptance, and what a looser rule would accept

**post-hoc analysis, NOT pre-registered: acceptance-rule variants re-evaluated on stored run graphs.** No new simulation; decision code unchanged (fingerprint `6406c53bb2011ef5`). Generated by `scripts/posthoc_acceptance_rule.py` on 2026-10-20T19:12:49+00:00.

## Rules compared

Tolerance τ = Cd 3%, St 3%; component pass limit 0.5 τ = τ/2.

- **V0, pre-registered** (`checks/verifier.aggregate`). Per quantity, each component (averaging, statistics, mesh, time, domain) must PASS: a mesh, time, domain or statistics component passes when its estimated relative uncertainty U ≤ τ/2; the averaging bias b passes when b ≤ τ (and FAILs above). The quantity is ACCEPT when every component passes and U_total = bias + RSS(other components) ≤ τ, REJECT when any component FAILs, INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. The case is ACCEPT when no check FAILs, every gate check passes or is discharged (Courant concern by a time PASS, first-order-scheme concern by a mesh PASS, for every quantity), and every quantity is ACCEPT.
- **V1, combined only.** A component that is INCONCLUSIVE only because U > τ/2 counts as measured; its U enters bias + RSS. ACCEPT when no component is FAIL, missing or unresolved for another reason, and bias + RSS ≤ τ.
- **V2, domain relaxed.** As V0, but the τ/2 limit is dropped for the domain component only.

Gate checks, FAIL criteria and the gate discharge rule are the same in all three; the variants change only which component results count as measured. Each variant is computed by the decision code's own `aggregate()` on copies of the replayed checks in which the relaxed component results are marked PASS.

**Criterion for 'INCONCLUSIVE only because U > τ/2'**: status INCONCLUSIVE with a numerical uncertainty attached. In the current decision code only two branches return that: the last branch of `sensitivity.assess_sequence` (U_root > τ/2 and the demonstrated change does not exceed τ by more than twice the statistical noise) and the u > τ/2 branch of `static.check_statistics`. Every other INCONCLUSIVE component result carries no uncertainty (no experiment, family member not statistically reliable, divergent sequence, no positive observed order, degenerate family, unknown temporal order, value missing, steady solver, too few cycles, unreliable averaging reference) and still blocks under V1 and V2. Every result treated this way has U above its threshold (checked).

True error e = (reported − T)/T against the in-house reference T (benchmark: `benchmark/labels.json`; attacks: the root run's `qoi.reported` against the same T).

**Labels.** Benchmark cases use both label views of `benchmark/labels.json` (with the truth-uncertainty mitigation / point estimates). These apply the narrow reading of the set-up clause of `docs/design.md` section 19: only set-up problems detected from the evidence (wrong Re, steady formulation) and missing quantities count; every other departure is judged by its error. Attack labels are computed as `scripts/analyze_benchmark.py` computes them for `results/benchmark/metrics.json`, in three readings: narrow (as the benchmark), literal (credible needs 'the set-up is consistent'; flawed needs e > τ or a set-up that 'answers a different problem (wrong Re or regime)') and set-up (any departure from the problem statement makes the case flawed). The counts below use the narrow views; false acceptances under the set-up reading are an extra column.

| attack | Cd error | St error | departure from the problem statement | narrow, with mitigation | narrow, point estimate | literal | set-up reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1_cylinder_geometry | +5.98% | -3.60% | cylinder diameter 1.05 D where the problem specifies D = 10 mm | flawed | flawed | flawed | flawed |
| X2_inlet_shear | +1.20% | -0.50% | sheared inlet profile where the problem specifies a uniform stream | ambiguous | credible | ambiguous | flawed |
| X3_compensating_errors | +5.81% | +0.16% | — (mesh and domain size only) | flawed | flawed | flawed | flawed |

X1 and X3 are flawed by their error in every reading (no set-up problem is detected from the evidence), so an acceptance of either is a false acceptance in every reading. X2 is flawed only under the set-up reading (sheared inlet profile where the problem specifies a uniform stream); under the narrow reading used by `benchmark/labels.json` and `metrics.json` it is ambiguous with mitigation and credible on point estimates, and ambiguous under the literal reading. No variant accepts the X2 case.

- All false case acceptances occur with verification v1 (`configs/verification.yaml`). With v2 the static geometry_consistency (X1) and inlet_uniformity (X2) checks FAIL, so B-v2 and C-rule-v2 REJECT X1 and X2 under every variant. These v2 checks were committed in 8161f5c (2026-10-19 07:40) before the attacks ran, but are post-hoc extensions of the pre-registered verifier (`configs/verification_v2.yaml` line 1): their detections of X1 and X2 are not blind tests. The X2 REJECTs are correct only under the set-up reading: under the narrow reading they are false rejections on point estimates and not scored with the mitigation (ambiguous under the literal reading too).

## Reproduction of the stored verdicts (V0)

V0 reproduces the stored case verdict, per-quantity verdict and combined U of all 137 results. For adaptive results V0 is INCONCLUSIVE at every intermediate state of the recorded loop, as it must be for the loop to have continued.

True errors and root runs of the benchmark results agree with `benchmark/labels.json` (checked).

## Summary per variant

Counts over the final evidence graph of each stored result. 'correct' = credible case ACCEPTed; 'false' = flawed case ACCEPTed; 'ambig.' = ambiguous case ACCEPTed (not scored). Each correct/false cell gives 'with mitigation · point estimate' in the narrow reading, each as ACCEPTed/labelled; 'ambig.' gives 'with mitigation · point estimate'. 'false, set-up reading' counts flawed cases ACCEPTed under the set-up reading, over attack cases only (benchmark labels use the narrow reading: —). Quantity columns count quantity-level ACCEPTs and those whose true error exceeds τ or τ/2 (the τ/2 count includes the τ count). 'loop ACCEPT' counts adaptive results whose recorded loop passes through a state the variant ACCEPTs (see the last section); '(flawed)' uses the narrow label with mitigation. All verdicts here are the deterministic verifier's. ¹ C-llm-v1+review: a verifier ACCEPT would go to the acceptance review, which was not run on these states, so the system's final verdict under V1 or V2 is unknown; its case ACCEPTs are counted as verifier ACCEPTs.

## What blocks acceptance under V0

INCONCLUSIVE quantities of cases whose V0 verdict is INCONCLUSIVE (in a REJECTed case the components do not decide the outcome), by the set of components that do not PASS. 'U>tau/2' = INCONCLUSIVE only because U exceeds τ/2. 'single run' = B, B-v1, B-v2 (no experiments by design); 'with experiments' = C-*, Bexh.

Over all results, 75 V0-INCONCLUSIVE quantities are blocked only by components with U > τ/2 (65 of them in INCONCLUSIVE cases); 38 of these become ACCEPT under V1, the others have bias + RSS > τ. 41 are blocked only by the domain component; 23 of these become ACCEPT under V2.

**Gates.** 24 V0-INCONCLUSIVE cases also hold a gate check that is neither passed nor discharged: physics_regime INCONCLUSIVE 16 (B/F1_upwind_convection, B/G1_premature_averaging, B/G2_average_from_start, C-rule/G1_premature_averaging, C-rule/G2_average_from_start, C-rule-prereg/F1_upwind_convection, C-rule-prereg/G1_premature_averaging, C-rule-prereg/G2_average_from_start, C-llm/G1_premature_averaging, C-llm/G2_average_from_start, Bexh/G1_premature_averaging, Bexh/G2_average_from_start, C-llm-r2/G1_premature_averaging, C-llm-r2/G2_average_from_start, C-llm-r3/G1_premature_averaging, C-llm-r3/G2_average_from_start); courant_number INCONCLUSIVE 8 (B/C1_large_timestep, B/C2_euler_large_timestep, C-rule/C2_euler_large_timestep, C-rule-prereg/C2_euler_large_timestep, C-llm/C2_euler_large_timestep, Bexh/C2_euler_large_timestep, C-llm-r2/C2_euler_large_timestep, C-llm-r3/C2_euler_large_timestep); convection_scheme_order INCONCLUSIVE 2 (B/F1_upwind_convection, C-rule-prereg/F1_upwind_convection). A case can hold more than one gate. No case has all quantities ACCEPT under V0, V1 or V2 while held by a gate: every gate-held case also has a quantity that is not ACCEPT under each variant, so it has component blockers as well.

## Adaptive loops: first state at which each rule is decisive

An adaptive loop stops at the first decisive verdict. The table lists adaptive results in which a variant is decisive at an earlier state of the recorded loop than V0, or with a different verdict ('state k' = root plus the first k experiments; the recorded loop ran to state n). This assumes the planner would have chosen the same experiments under the variant, which is not guaranteed. For C-llm-v1+review an ACCEPT would go to the acceptance review.
